topics: Data Collection and Reporting in Community Health
Use of Technology in Community Nursing

questions.question_text: Which of the following best describes planning as a function of nursing management?

choices.text: Assigning duties to staff members according to their roles
Determining objectives and deciding in advance how to achieve them
Evaluating staff performance against established standards
Motivating staff to carry out assigned responsibilities

questions.rationale: Planning involves setting objectives, identifying priorities and determining the activities and resources required to achieve desired outcomes. It provides direction for other management functions.

questions.question_text: Which management function involves grouping activities, assigning responsibilities and establishing working relationships?

choices.text: Planning
Organizing
Controlling
Evaluating

questions.rationale: Organizing involves arranging tasks, personnel and resources to accomplish established objectives. It clarifies responsibilities and reporting relationships within a health facility.

questions.question_text: In nursing management, directing primarily involves which activity?

choices.text: Developing the annual budget
Guiding, supervising and motivating staff
Preparing monthly morbidity statistics
Comparing expenditure with the approved budget

questions.rationale: Directing is the management function concerned with providing leadership, guidance, communication and motivation. It helps staff understand and perform their assigned responsibilities.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best explains the controlling function of nursing management?

choices.text: Recruiting additional health workers
Setting the objectives of a community programme
Monitoring performance and correcting deviations from standards
Distributing duties among community health nurses

questions.rationale: Controlling involves measuring actual performance, comparing it with established standards and taking corrective action where necessary. It helps ensure that nursing activities achieve their intended objectives.

questions.question_text: Which leadership style encourages team members to participate in decision-making?

choices.text: Autocratic leadership
Democratic leadership
Laissez-faire leadership
Bureaucratic leadership

questions.rationale: Democratic leadership involves consultation and participation of team members in decision-making. It can improve staff commitment, communication and cooperation.

questions.question_text: What is delegation in nursing?

choices.text: Transferring all professional accountability to another worker
Assigning a task to a competent person while retaining appropriate accountability
Allowing every staff member to perform any clinical procedure
Avoiding responsibility for activities performed by junior staff

questions.rationale: Delegation is the assignment of responsibility for performing a specific task to a person with the necessary competence. The nurse who delegates remains accountable for the appropriateness of the delegation and the required supervision.

questions.question_text: Which principle should guide a community health nurse when prioritizing competing patient-care activities?

choices.text: Completing the easiest activity first
Attending to patients according to clinical urgency and risk
Serving patients in the order of their social status
Performing administrative duties before urgent clinical care

questions.rationale: Clinical prioritization is based on the severity of a patient's condition, the risk of deterioration and the potential consequences of delay. Urgent threats to life and safety take precedence over routine activities.

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of maintaining accurate patient records?

choices.text: To provide evidence of care and support continuity of treatment
To replace communication between healthcare professionals
To prevent patients from accessing their health information
To record only the financial transactions of the facility

questions.rationale: Patient records provide a documented account of assessment, care, treatment and outcomes. They support continuity of care, clinical communication, accountability, audit and appropriate decision-making.

questions.question_text: Which documentation practice is most appropriate when recording nursing care?

choices.text: Recording care at the end of the month
Using vague expressions to save time
Making timely, accurate, objective and legible entries
Documenting interventions before they are performed

questions.rationale: Nursing documentation should accurately reflect the care provided and the patient's response. Entries should be timely, objective, complete and attributable to the person making them.

questions.question_text: What is health informatics?

choices.text: The study of hospital building design
The application of information and communication technologies to health information and healthcare
The process of diagnosing diseases without patient assessment
The management of medical equipment without using information

questions.rationale: Health informatics combines health sciences, information science and technology to collect, manage, analyse and use health information. It supports clinical care, public health, administration and health-system decision-making.

questions.question_text: What does the abbreviation EHR represent in healthcare informatics?

choices.text: Electronic Health Record
Emergency Hospital Register
External Health Referral
Electronic Hospital Revenue

questions.rationale: An Electronic Health Record is a digital record of a patient's health information maintained for use by authorised healthcare professionals. It can support documentation, clinical decision-making and continuity of care.

questions.question_text: In Ghana's health information system, what is the main purpose of DHIMS2?

choices.text: To issue professional licences to nurses
To manage the payroll of all health workers
To collect, manage, analyse and report routine health-service data
To replace all patient consultations with online services

questions.rationale: DHIMS2 is used for routine health information management, including the aggregation, analysis and reporting of health-service data. The information supports monitoring, planning and decision-making at different levels of the health system.

questions.topic: Data Collection and Reporting in Community Health
questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of primary data collection in community health nursing?

choices.text: Reviewing a published national health report
Interviewing a household during a community home visit
Reading a previous district annual report
Using an existing journal article on malaria

questions.rationale: Primary data are collected directly from original sources for a specific purpose. Interviewing a household during a home visit is a direct method of obtaining information from community members.

questions.question_text: What does confidentiality mean in the management of patient information?

choices.text: Making all patient records available to the public
Protecting patient information from unauthorised access or disclosure
Allowing staff to discuss patient details in public places
Deleting all patient records after every consultation

questions.rationale: Confidentiality is the duty to protect private patient information from inappropriate access, use or disclosure. Information should be shared only with authorised persons for legitimate purposes, subject to applicable legal and professional requirements.

questions.question_text: What is a nursing audit?

choices.text: A systematic examination of nursing practice or records against established standards
A method of recruiting nurses for a health facility
A process of issuing medicines to patients
An informal discussion unrelated to care standards

questions.rationale: A nursing audit systematically evaluates the quality of nursing care by examining practice, documentation or outcomes against agreed standards. Findings can identify gaps and guide improvements in service delivery.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of a material resource in a CHPS compound?

choices.text: Community health nurse
Monthly operational budget
Blood pressure monitoring equipment
Leadership and supervision

questions.rationale: Material resources are physical supplies and equipment used to deliver healthcare services. Examples include blood pressure monitors, weighing scales, vaccines, stationery and clinical consumables.

questions.question_text: A community health nurse in charge prepares a weekly duty roster and assigns specific responsibilities to team members. Which management function is being demonstrated?

choices.text: Organizing
Controlling
Auditing
Budgeting

questions.rationale: Preparing a duty roster and allocating responsibilities are organizing activities because they arrange personnel and tasks to achieve service objectives. Clear allocation of duties also helps prevent duplication and omissions.

questions.question_text: A CHPS compound has recorded an increase in childhood malaria cases. The community health officer sets a target to reduce cases through health education and environmental sanitation activities. Which management function is primarily demonstrated?

choices.text: Controlling
Planning
Directing
Staff appraisal

questions.rationale: The officer is identifying a problem, setting an objective and determining interventions to achieve a desired outcome. These activities are central to the planning function of management.

questions.question_text: During a monthly review, a community health officer discovers that only 60% of the planned home visits were completed. What should the officer do as part of the controlling function?

choices.text: Ignore the difference because some visits were completed
Compare performance with the target, identify causes and take corrective action
Immediately dismiss the staff responsible
Change the recorded target to match the completed visits

questions.rationale: Controlling requires comparing actual performance with planned standards and identifying reasons for any deviation. Appropriate corrective action should then be taken to improve performance.

questions.question_text: A nurse in charge asks a trained community health nurse to conduct an approved health education session on malaria prevention while the officer attends a district meeting. Which action best demonstrates appropriate delegation?

choices.text: Giving the task without explaining the expected outcome
Confirming the staff member's competence, clarifying the task and arranging appropriate follow-up
Transferring all responsibility for the CHPS compound to the staff member
Asking an untrained volunteer to perform any clinical procedure required

questions.rationale: Appropriate delegation requires matching the task to the person's competence and scope of practice. The nurse should communicate expectations and provide supervision or follow-up appropriate to the task.

questions.question_text: A newly posted nurse is unfamiliar with the reporting procedure at a district hospital. Which leadership action by the supervisor is most appropriate?

choices.text: Criticising the nurse for asking questions
Providing orientation, guidance and opportunities to clarify the procedure
Allowing the nurse to develop an independent reporting system
Withholding all reporting responsibilities indefinitely

questions.rationale: Orientation and supportive supervision help newly posted staff understand workplace procedures and expected standards. This approach promotes competence, confidence and accurate reporting.

questions.question_text: A community health nurse arrives at a household for a routine visit and finds a child who is unconscious and breathing abnormally. What should the nurse do first?

choices.text: Complete the household registration form
Assess the child's immediate condition, initiate appropriate emergency care and arrange urgent referral
Continue the scheduled health education session
Ask the caregiver to bring the child to the CHPS compound the following day

questions.rationale: Unconsciousness with abnormal breathing indicates a potentially life-threatening emergency requiring immediate assessment and intervention. Routine documentation and health education must be postponed while emergency care and urgent referral are arranged.

questions.question_text: A nurse at a CHPS compound has four activities to complete. Which activity should receive the highest priority?

choices.text: Preparing the monthly summary report
Rearranging the filing cabinet
Assessing a patient with severe difficulty in breathing
Preparing notices for an upcoming health education programme

questions.rationale: Severe difficulty in breathing may indicate an immediate threat to life and requires urgent clinical assessment and intervention. Administrative and organisational tasks can be completed after the patient's immediate needs are addressed.

questions.question_text: A community health nurse has several scheduled home visits but receives information that a pregnant woman in the community is experiencing heavy vaginal bleeding. What is the most appropriate action?

choices.text: Complete the scheduled visits before responding
Prioritise the emergency, assess the woman and arrange immediate referral to an appropriate facility
Advise the woman to rest and report the bleeding at the next antenatal clinic
Ask another household to monitor the woman without contacting a health facility

questions.rationale: Heavy vaginal bleeding during pregnancy is an obstetric danger sign that may threaten the life of the woman and fetus. The nurse should prioritise prompt assessment, emergency management within competence and urgent referral.

questions.question_text: A nurse has to prepare a report, attend a routine meeting and provide care to a patient who suddenly develops signs of severe dehydration. Which activity should be performed first?

choices.text: Attend the routine meeting
Complete the report
Assess and initiate appropriate management of the patient's condition
Arrange the next week's duty roster

questions.rationale: Severe dehydration can rapidly progress to shock and requires prompt assessment and treatment. Routine administrative activities should be deferred until the patient's immediate clinical needs have been addressed.

questions.question_text: During a home visit, a nurse assesses a client with hypertension and records the blood pressure, medication history and health education provided. Which documentation principle is being applied?

choices.text: Completeness and accuracy
Confidentiality through omission of clinical findings
Retrospective documentation
Informal verbal reporting

questions.rationale: Recording relevant assessment findings, medication history and interventions provides a complete account of the care delivered. Accurate documentation supports follow-up, continuity of care and clinical decision-making.

questions.question_text: A nurse makes an error while writing in a paper patient record. What is the appropriate way to correct the error?

choices.text: Erase the incorrect entry completely
Cover the error with correction fluid
Draw a single line through the error, make the correct entry and authenticate the correction according to policy
Remove the entire page from the patient's file

questions.rationale: A correction should preserve the original entry so that the record remains transparent and auditable. The correction should be clearly identified, dated or timed and authenticated in accordance with facility documentation policy.

questions.question_text: A community health nurse refers a patient with suspected tuberculosis from a CHPS compound to a district hospital. Which information is most important to include in the referral documentation?

choices.text: Only the patient's name and community
Relevant history, assessment findings, reason for referral and care already provided
The nurse's personal opinion about the patient's behaviour
Only the date on which the patient first visited the CHPS compound

questions.rationale: A useful referral record communicates the clinical information needed for continued assessment and management. Relevant history, findings, interventions and the reason for referral support continuity and patient safety.

questions.question_text: A district hospital introduces an electronic health record system. Which activity is an appropriate use of the system by an authorised nurse?

choices.text: Recording patient assessment findings and nursing interventions
Allowing visitors to browse patient records
Sharing the nurse's login credentials with colleagues
Deleting a patient's history to create storage space

questions.rationale: An EHR allows authorised healthcare professionals to document and retrieve relevant patient information electronically. Access and use must follow professional responsibilities, facility procedures and information security requirements.

questions.question_text: A community health nurse enters routine service statistics into DHIMS2 after checking the facility's source registers. Why is this verification important?

choices.text: It makes the reporting process unnecessary
It helps improve the accuracy and consistency of reported data
It allows the nurse to estimate missing figures without documentation
It prevents district health managers from reviewing the data

questions.rationale: Checking source registers before data entry helps identify omissions, inconsistencies and recording errors. Accurate data are essential for reliable analysis, planning and monitoring of health services.

questions.topic: Data Collection and Reporting in Community Health
questions.question_text: During a household survey, a community health nurse collects information on the number of children who have received routine immunisation. Which data collection method is most appropriate?

choices.text: Structured interview using a standardised questionnaire
Informal discussion without recording responses
Guessing the number based on the size of the household
Using unrelated hospital financial records

questions.rationale: A structured questionnaire provides a consistent method of collecting information from households. Standardised questions improve comparability and make the data easier to analyse.

questions.topic: Data Collection and Reporting in Community Health
questions.question_text: A CHPS compound records 24 new malaria cases among children during a reporting month. What should the nurse do before submitting the monthly report?

choices.text: Double the figure to account for unreported cases
Check the source records and ensure that the reported figure is complete and accurate
Remove cases that were treated successfully
Replace the figure with the previous month's total

questions.rationale: Monthly reports should be based on verified source data and should accurately reflect the reporting period. Figures should not be altered through unsupported estimates or assumptions.

questions.question_text: A nurse uses a computer to access an electronic patient record at a district hospital. What should the nurse do before leaving the workstation unattended?

choices.text: Leave the patient record open for the next staff member
Log out or lock the workstation
Write the password on the computer monitor
Allow other patients to use the active session

questions.rationale: Logging out or locking the workstation prevents unauthorised persons from accessing confidential patient information. Individual user accounts also support accountability by linking system activities to authorised users.

questions.question_text: A community health nurse is asked by a neighbour to disclose the HIV status of a person receiving care at the CHPS compound. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Disclose the information because the neighbour lives in the same community
Refuse to disclose the information and protect the patient's confidentiality
Confirm the diagnosis but avoid mentioning the patient's name
Share the information if the neighbour promises not to tell anyone

questions.rationale: A patient's HIV status is confidential health information and should not be disclosed to an unauthorised person. Disclosure must follow applicable legal and professional requirements and should not be based on community curiosity or informal requests.

questions.topic: Use of Technology in Community Nursing
questions.question_text: A community health nurse uses a mobile phone to send appointment reminders to clients who have agreed to receive them. Which benefit of mHealth is being demonstrated?

choices.text: Improved communication and follow-up with clients
Elimination of the need for clinical assessment
Automatic replacement of all community health workers
Removal of the need to protect personal information

questions.rationale: Mobile health technologies can support reminders, health education, communication and follow-up. Their use should respect consent, confidentiality and the limitations of mobile communication.

questions.topic: Use of Technology in Community Nursing
questions.question_text: A CHPS compound experiences an internet outage while the nurse is conducting a community health activity. Which action is most appropriate?

choices.text: Stop all patient care until internet service returns
Use approved downtime procedures and secure records for later entry or synchronisation
Enter patient information into an unprotected public online form
Discard all information collected during the outage

questions.rationale: Patient care should continue using approved alternative procedures when digital systems are unavailable. Information should be documented securely and entered or synchronised later according to facility policy.

questions.question_text: A CHPS compound discovers that many children miss scheduled immunisation appointments. Which action is the best first step in a quality improvement process?

choices.text: Immediately blame the vaccination staff
Collect and review information to identify possible causes of missed appointments
Stop providing immunisation services
Change the immunisation schedule without reviewing the problem

questions.rationale: Quality improvement begins with understanding the problem and examining relevant evidence. Identifying causes, such as access barriers or ineffective reminders, helps the team select appropriate interventions.

questions.question_text: A nurse in charge conducts an audit of patient records and finds that vital signs are frequently missing. What is the most appropriate response?

choices.text: Ignore the omissions because the patients were discharged
Provide feedback, reinforce documentation standards and re-audit practice
Complete all missing entries using estimated values
Destroy the records containing omissions

questions.rationale: Audit findings should be used to identify gaps and guide corrective action, such as staff education and supervision. Re-auditing helps determine whether the improvement measures have been effective.

questions.question_text: A CHPS compound has a limited supply of gloves, disinfectant and wound dressings. Which management action is most appropriate?

choices.text: Use supplies without recording their consumption
Prioritise essential clinical needs, monitor stock and request replenishment through the appropriate channel
Stop all services until the next annual budget
Distribute supplies equally without considering clinical needs

questions.rationale: Effective resource management requires monitoring stock levels and allocating supplies according to service needs and safety requirements. Timely replenishment helps prevent stock-outs and interruptions in care.

questions.question_text: A community health officer is preparing a budget for a malaria prevention outreach programme. Which item should be included as a financial resource requirement?

choices.text: The number of nurses assigned to the programme
The cost of transport, educational materials and approved supplies
The professional qualifications of the outreach team
The number of households in the community

questions.rationale: A budget estimates the financial resources required to carry out planned activities. Costs such as transport, materials and supplies should be identified to support realistic programme implementation.

questions.question_text: A nurse in charge notices that a weighing scale at the CHPS compound is giving inconsistent readings. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Continue using it and record whichever reading appears first
Remove it from clinical use until it has been checked, calibrated or repaired as appropriate
Ask patients to estimate their own weight
Adjust the readings manually without checking the equipment

questions.rationale: Inaccurate equipment can lead to incorrect clinical assessments and decisions. The scale should be checked and appropriately maintained before it is used for patient care again.

questions.question_text: During a community outreach programme, a nurse assigns a trained community health volunteer to guide residents to the registration point. Which consideration is most important when making this assignment?

choices.text: Whether the volunteer can perform every nursing procedure
Whether the assigned activity is appropriate to the volunteer's training and role
Whether the volunteer has the longest period of service in the community
Whether the volunteer can independently make clinical diagnoses

questions.rationale: Delegated activities must be appropriate to the person's competence, training and permitted role. Clinical assessment and interventions requiring professional nursing judgement must remain with appropriately qualified personnel.

questions.topic: Data Collection and Reporting in Community Health
questions.question_text: A nurse is conducting a household survey on access to safe drinking water. Which practice will most improve the reliability of the collected information?

choices.text: Asking different households completely different questions
Using clear, standardised questions and recording responses consistently
Recording only responses that support the nurse's expectations
Completing questionnaires from memory several weeks later

questions.rationale: Standardised questions and consistent recording reduce variation introduced by the data collector. This improves the comparability and reliability of information obtained from different households.

questions.question_text: A district health director wants to compare malaria trends across several CHPS zones using DHIMS2 reports. Which use of the system best supports this activity?

choices.text: Analysing aggregated routine health data across reporting locations and periods
Accessing the private passwords of community health nurses
Replacing all household visits with computer-generated estimates
Deleting reports from facilities with low attendance

questions.rationale: DHIMS2 supports the aggregation and analysis of routine health-service information across facilities and reporting periods. Comparing these data can help identify trends and guide public health planning.

questions.question_text: A nurse receives an email requesting the password used to access the hospital's electronic patient record system. The message claims to be from technical support. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Send the password immediately to avoid account suspension
Avoid sharing the password and verify the request through an authorised support channel
Forward the password to other nurses for confirmation
Use the same password for all hospital systems

questions.rationale: Requests for passwords may be phishing attempts intended to obtain unauthorised access. Credentials should remain private, and suspicious requests should be verified and reported through approved channels.

questions.question_text: A nurse has planned a community education session, but heavy rainfall has made the usual access road unsafe. What is the best time-management response?

choices.text: Proceed regardless of the safety risk
Reassess the situation, communicate changes and reschedule or use a safe alternative
Cancel all future community education activities
Travel alone through the unsafe route to avoid delay

questions.rationale: Effective time management includes adapting plans when circumstances change while maintaining safety and service objectives. Communicating and arranging a safe alternative prevents unnecessary risk and confusion.

questions.question_text: A nurse receives a patient from another facility and notices that the referral note is incomplete. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Assume that all missing information is normal
Assess the patient, obtain relevant information from appropriate sources and document the findings
Refuse to provide care until a perfect referral note is received
Invent missing clinical details to complete the record

questions.rationale: Patient assessment and safe continuity of care should not depend solely on the completeness of a referral note. The nurse should obtain and document relevant information without fabricating details.

questions.question_text: A CHPS team introduces a checklist to improve the completeness of antenatal care documentation. Which indicator would best measure the effectiveness of this intervention?

choices.text: The number of chairs in the antenatal clinic
The proportion of reviewed antenatal records with all required fields completed
The number of staff who attended the last district meeting
The distance between the CHPS compound and the district hospital

questions.rationale: The proportion of records with required fields completed directly measures documentation completeness. Comparing this indicator before and after the checklist intervention helps evaluate improvement.

questions.topic: Use of Technology in Community Nursing
questions.question_text: A community health nurse uses a mobile application to record household visits while working in an area with intermittent network coverage. Which approach is most appropriate?

choices.text: Use an approved application with secure offline data capture and later synchronisation
Store all patient details in an unrestricted social media account
Share the device password with every household visited
Delete the records whenever the network becomes unavailable

questions.rationale: Approved applications with secure offline functionality can support data collection in areas with unreliable connectivity. Data should be protected during storage and synchronised according to authorised procedures.

questions.question_text: A CHPS compound has only one functional blood pressure monitor, and several nurses need to use it during clinic hours. What is the most appropriate management action?

choices.text: Allow staff to take the equipment home without recording it
Coordinate its use, maintain an equipment register and report the need for additional equipment
Prevent other nurses from providing services
Purchase a replacement without following procurement procedures

questions.rationale: Coordinating equipment use helps maintain service delivery while ensuring that the available resource is accounted for. Reporting the shortage through appropriate channels supports procurement and resource planning.

questions.question_text: A nurse in charge notices that staff members are unclear about who should submit the weekly community health report. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Allow every staff member to submit a separate report
Clarify reporting responsibilities and establish a clear communication procedure
Stop collecting community health data
Wait until the district office complains about missing reports

questions.rationale: Clear allocation of responsibilities and communication procedures are essential for effective organisation and coordination. Clarifying who prepares, checks and submits reports reduces duplication and missed deadlines.

questions.question_text: A nurse in charge asks a staff member to perform a procedure that the staff member has not been trained to undertake. What should the staff member do?

choices.text: Perform the procedure to avoid displeasing the supervisor
Explain the limitation, decline the unsafe assignment and seek an appropriately qualified practitioner
Ask a patient to assist with the procedure
Perform the procedure without supervision and document it as routine

questions.rationale: Nurses must practise within their competence and professional scope. An assignment that cannot be performed safely should be raised promptly so that appropriate care can be arranged.

questions.topic: Data Collection and Reporting in Community Health
questions.question_text: A nurse reviewing the CHPS monthly report finds that the number of immunisation visits is higher than the number recorded in the source register. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Submit the higher figure because it shows improved performance
Reconcile the report with the source register and correct any verified discrepancy
Delete the source register
Use the average of the two figures without investigation

questions.rationale: Differences between summary reports and source records should be investigated before submission. Reconciliation helps maintain data accuracy and prevents misleading service statistics.

questions.question_text: A nurse wants to discuss a patient's clinical condition with another healthcare professional involved in the patient's care. Which action is appropriate?

choices.text: Discuss the case in a public transport vehicle
Share only relevant information through an appropriate confidential channel
Post the patient's details in a general community WhatsApp group
Send the entire patient file to an unrelated staff member

questions.rationale: Relevant patient information may be shared with authorised professionals when necessary for legitimate care purposes. The information should be limited to what is needed and communicated through secure, appropriate channels.

questions.question_text: During a community outreach programme, a nurse is informed that a child has developed convulsions. What should the nurse do first?

choices.text: Continue registering other participants
Ensure the child's immediate safety, assess the condition and arrange urgent emergency care
Ask the caregiver to wait until the outreach programme ends
Complete the outreach attendance report

questions.rationale: Convulsions in a child require immediate assessment and protection from injury, followed by appropriate emergency management and referral. Administrative activities must not delay urgent care.

questions.question_text: A district hospital introduces a new patient identification procedure after an audit identifies frequent identification errors. Which action best supports implementation?

choices.text: Assume that staff will understand the procedure without explanation
Orient staff, monitor compliance and review incidents after implementation
Remove patient identification checks during busy periods
Evaluate the procedure only when another serious error occurs

questions.rationale: Effective implementation requires staff orientation, monitoring and evaluation of practice. Reviewing compliance and incidents helps determine whether the new procedure improves patient safety.

questions.question_text: A community health nurse uses a digital tool to calculate the proportion of children who completed their scheduled immunisation. Which informatics function is being demonstrated?

choices.text: Data analysis
Physical filing
Clinical delegation
Equipment maintenance

questions.rationale: Data analysis involves processing and interpreting collected information to produce meaningful indicators. Calculating immunisation coverage helps the team assess programme performance and identify service gaps.

questions.question_text: A community health officer is planning a home-visit programme for older adults with chronic conditions. Which approach best demonstrates effective planning?

choices.text: Scheduling visits without considering staff availability or community needs
Identifying the target population, setting objectives, allocating resources and preparing a schedule
Waiting until all patients independently request a visit
Assigning all visits to one nurse regardless of workload

questions.rationale: Effective planning considers the population's needs, programme objectives, available personnel and resources. A realistic schedule helps ensure that home visits are delivered systematically and equitably.

questions.question_text: A patient receiving treatment for hypertension tells the community health nurse that the prescribed medication causes dizziness. Which action should be documented?

choices.text: Only the patient's name and date of visit
The patient's report, relevant assessment findings, advice or intervention and follow-up plan
The nurse's assumption that the patient is not taking medication
A statement that the medication has been discontinued without an authorised decision

questions.rationale: The record should capture the patient's reported concern, relevant findings and actions taken. Accurate documentation supports clinical review, medication safety and continuity of care.

questions.question_text: At a community clinic, a patient suddenly collapses while several clients are waiting for routine services. What should the nurse do first?

choices.text: Continue serving clients according to the queue
Assess responsiveness and breathing, call for assistance and initiate appropriate emergency care
Ask the patient to wait until the consultation room is free
Complete the daily attendance register

questions.rationale: A sudden collapse may indicate a life-threatening emergency and requires immediate assessment. Calling for assistance and initiating appropriate emergency care take priority over routine clinic activities.

questions.question_text: A nurse uses a personal smartphone to take a photograph of a patient's wound for clinical consultation. Which action is most appropriate?

choices.text: Take the photograph and upload it to a public social media account
Follow facility policy, obtain appropriate consent and use an approved secure method for handling the image
Send the photograph to several friends for their opinions
Include the patient's name and contact details in an open online discussion

questions.rationale: Clinical photographs contain identifiable or sensitive health information and require appropriate safeguards. Consent, authorised clinical purpose, secure storage and approved communication procedures should be observed.

questions.question_text: A community health team wants to determine whether health education has improved handwashing practices among households. Which evaluation method is most appropriate?

choices.text: Assuming that attendance at the education session proves behaviour change
Assessing handwashing knowledge and practices before and after the intervention
Counting only the number of posters distributed
Measuring the number of staff who prepared the session

questions.rationale: Evaluating knowledge and observed practices provides information about whether the intervention has influenced its intended outcomes. Attendance and materials distributed measure activities or outputs rather than actual behaviour change.

questions.question_text: Two nurses disagree about the allocation of duties during a busy immunisation session. What should the nurse in charge do?

choices.text: Ignore the disagreement and allow the conflict to continue
Listen to both nurses, clarify responsibilities and agree on a safe allocation of duties
Publicly embarrass both nurses in front of patients
Cancel the immunisation session immediately

questions.rationale: Constructive conflict management involves listening, clarifying expectations and finding a practical solution. Clear responsibilities help maintain teamwork and prevent disruption of patient care.

questions.question_text: A nurse uses an electronic system to review a patient's previous consultations before providing care. Which benefit of an EHR is most directly demonstrated?

choices.text: Improved access to relevant patient information for continuity of care
Elimination of the need for patient consent in every situation
Automatic prevention of all clinical errors
Removal of the need for accurate documentation

questions.rationale: An EHR can make relevant patient information available to authorised healthcare professionals across encounters. This supports continuity and informed clinical decisions, although it does not eliminate the need for professional judgement or accurate records.

questions.question_text: A district nursing supervisor introduces a new reporting target but does not explain it to the community health team. Staff members submit reports using different formats. Which management function was inadequately performed?

choices.text: Directing
Controlling
Budgeting
Auditing

questions.rationale: Directing includes communicating instructions, providing guidance and ensuring that staff understand expected performance. The lack of explanation contributed to inconsistent implementation of the reporting requirement.

questions.question_text: A CHPS compound has a plan to conduct 100 household visits in a month. At the end of the month, only 45 visits have been completed. Staff report that the vehicle was unavailable for two weeks and the visit schedule was not adjusted. Which management weakness is most evident?

choices.text: Failure to establish objectives
Inadequate monitoring and adjustment of implementation
Excessive delegation to qualified staff
Overuse of electronic health records

questions.rationale: The target was established, but the programme was not adequately monitored or adjusted when a major resource constraint occurred. Effective management requires identifying implementation barriers and taking corrective action to keep activities on track.

questions.question_text: A nurse in charge delegates the preparation of a monthly health report to a junior nurse but does not explain the reporting requirements or check the final document. The report contains major errors. Which conclusion is most appropriate?

choices.text: Delegation is inappropriate in all nursing situations
The delegation process was incomplete because instructions and appropriate follow-up were lacking
The junior nurse alone must be responsible for every aspect of the failure
Monthly reports do not require verification

questions.rationale: Effective delegation requires clear instructions, an appropriate match between task and competence, and suitable supervision or review. The nurse in charge should ensure that the delegated task is completed to the required standard.

questions.question_text: At a CHPS compound, four patients arrive at the same time. Patient 1 has mild headache, Patient 2 has severe difficulty breathing, Patient 3 requires routine medication refill, and Patient 4 has a minor skin rash. Which patient should be assessed first?

choices.text: Patient 1
Patient 2
Patient 3
Patient 4

questions.rationale: Severe difficulty breathing indicates a potentially life-threatening problem requiring immediate assessment and intervention. The other patients have needs that appear less urgent based on the information provided.

questions.question_text: A community health nurse is conducting a home visit when the caregiver reports that a child has had profuse watery diarrhoea and is now lethargic with sunken eyes. What is the priority action?

choices.text: Complete the routine household health assessment before taking action
Assess for severe dehydration, begin appropriate emergency rehydration within the nurse's competence and arrange urgent referral
Advise the caregiver to stop giving the child fluids
Schedule a follow-up visit for the next week

questions.rationale: Lethargy and sunken eyes in a child with profuse diarrhoea are concerning signs of dehydration that may be severe. Immediate assessment, appropriate rehydration and urgent referral are required rather than routine follow-up.

questions.question_text: A nurse reviews a patient's record and discovers that a medication administration entry has been signed, although the patient states that the medication was not given. What is the most appropriate response?

choices.text: Ignore the discrepancy because the record has already been signed
Establish the facts promptly, assess the patient, report the discrepancy through the appropriate process and ensure accurate documentation
Delete the signed entry without explanation
Administer an additional dose immediately without checking the prescription or timing

questions.rationale: A discrepancy between the record and the patient's account may indicate a medication safety incident and requires prompt investigation. The nurse should assess potential harm, follow reporting procedures and ensure that the record accurately reflects verified facts.

questions.question_text: A district hospital has both paper records and an EHR. A nurse finds that the patient's allergy information differs between the two systems. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Choose whichever record is easier to access
Verify the allergy information with the patient and appropriate clinical sources, then follow the facility's correction and escalation procedure
Delete the allergy information from both systems
Ignore the discrepancy because allergies are not relevant to treatment

questions.rationale: Conflicting allergy information creates a potential patient safety risk, particularly when medicines are prescribed or administered. The nurse should verify the information and ensure that corrections are made through authorised procedures so that the record remains reliable.

questions.topic: Data Collection and Reporting in Community Health
questions.question_text: A CHPS compound reports a sudden increase in malaria cases. However, the number of cases in the source register is much lower than the figure entered into DHIMS2. Which action should the nurse in charge take?

choices.text: Accept the DHIMS2 figure because electronic data are always correct
Investigate the discrepancy by checking source documents, reporting-period definitions and data-entry records before correcting the report
Delete all malaria records from the reporting period
Use the higher figure to attract additional resources without verification

questions.rationale: A difference between source records and reported data may result from duplicate entries, incorrect aggregation or data-entry errors. Verification is necessary before the information is used for surveillance, planning or resource allocation.

questions.question_text: A community health nurse discovers that a colleague has posted a photograph of a patient record in a WhatsApp group containing people who are not involved in the patient's care. What is the most appropriate response?

choices.text: Forward the photograph to other groups for awareness
Take prompt steps through the appropriate reporting process to contain the disclosure and protect the patient's information
Ignore the incident because the group is private
Publicly identify the patient to explain why the disclosure is wrong

questions.rationale: Sharing identifiable patient information with unauthorised persons is a confidentiality breach, even when the platform is a private group. The incident should be reported through appropriate channels so that further disclosure can be limited and the patient's privacy protected.

questions.question_text: An audit at a district hospital shows that patient records frequently lack documentation of pain assessment. Staff receive training, but a second audit shows no improvement. What should the quality improvement team do next?

choices.text: Conclude that documentation standards are unnecessary
Investigate barriers to compliance and revise the improvement strategy based on the findings
Stop auditing patient records
Complete missing pain assessments retrospectively without assessing patients

questions.rationale: The absence of improvement suggests that training alone may not have addressed the underlying barriers. The team should investigate factors such as workflow, forms, workload and supervision before selecting further interventions.

questions.question_text: A CHPS compound repeatedly runs out of essential wound-care supplies before the end of each month. Stock records show that consumption is higher than the quantity requested during procurement. Which management response is most appropriate?

choices.text: Continue requesting the same quantity because it was previously approved
Review consumption patterns, check stock records and adjust future requests through approved procurement procedures
Stop recording the use of wound-care materials
Use expired supplies to avoid further stock-outs

questions.rationale: Repeated stock-outs indicate that procurement estimates may not reflect actual consumption or changing service needs. Reviewing reliable stock and usage data supports more accurate forecasting and responsible resource allocation.

questions.question_text: A nurse in charge assigns a community health volunteer to independently assess pregnant women and decide which ones require emergency referral. The volunteer has received only basic community mobilisation training. Which judgement is most appropriate?

choices.text: The assignment is appropriate because volunteers know the community
The assignment is unsafe because it requires clinical assessment and judgement beyond the volunteer's competence
The assignment is appropriate if the volunteer has completed secondary school
The assignment is acceptable if the nurse reviews the cases at the end of the month

questions.rationale: Recognising obstetric complications and deciding on emergency referral require appropriate clinical competence. Community volunteers may support mobilisation and referral communication, but they should not be assigned independent clinical decisions beyond their training and role.

questions.question_text: A nurse at a community clinic must respond to four situations: a patient with severe chest pain and sweating, a client requesting a routine blood pressure check, a caregiver seeking a child welfare appointment and a staff member requesting help with filing. Which action should be prioritised?

choices.text: Help the staff member complete filing
Assess the patient with severe chest pain and sweating and activate urgent emergency care
Arrange the child welfare appointment
Perform the routine blood pressure check first

questions.rationale: Severe chest pain accompanied by sweating may indicate an acute coronary event or another serious emergency. Immediate assessment and urgent escalation take precedence over routine services and administrative work.

questions.topic: Data Collection and Reporting in Community Health
questions.question_text: A district health team notices that one CHPS zone reports almost no maternal deaths, while another reports a sudden increase. The team suspects differences in case identification and reporting practices. What is the best analytical response?

choices.text: Assume that the zone reporting fewer deaths has better maternal health services
Review case definitions, reporting completeness and source records across both zones before comparing the figures
Remove the zone with higher figures from the district report
Average the two figures without examining their quality

questions.rationale: Differences in reporting completeness or case identification can distort comparisons between health zones. The team should assess data quality and consistency before drawing conclusions about actual maternal health outcomes.

questions.topic: Use of Technology in Community Nursing
questions.question_text: A community health team uses a mobile application to collect household health information. During review, the supervisor discovers that several records were uploaded twice after network reconnection. What is the most appropriate response?

choices.text: Delete all household records from the application
Identify and reconcile duplicate records using approved procedures while preserving the accuracy and audit trail of the data
Count duplicate records as additional households reached
Ignore the duplicates because they do not affect data quality

questions.rationale: Duplicate records can inflate service statistics and produce inaccurate reports. The team should identify duplicates, reconcile them using authorised procedures and preserve appropriate records of corrections.

questions.question_text: A nurse in charge observes that staff attendance is satisfactory, but patient waiting times remain high and complaints are increasing. Which management response is most appropriate?

choices.text: Assume that staff attendance alone proves that the service is effective
Review patient flow, workload distribution and service processes to identify causes of delay
Increase staff attendance requirements without examining service delivery
Stop collecting patient feedback

questions.rationale: Staff attendance is only one aspect of service performance and does not establish that patient care is efficient. Reviewing workflow, workload and patient feedback can identify operational problems requiring corrective action.

questions.question_text: A nurse accidentally sends a patient's laboratory result to the wrong recipient by email. Which response best addresses the incident?

choices.text: Ignore the mistake because the email has already been sent
Promptly report the incident through the appropriate channel, attempt to limit further disclosure and follow the facility's breach-response procedure
Send the same result to several other recipients to correct the mistake
Delete the patient's record from the hospital system

questions.rationale: Sending a patient's result to an unauthorised recipient is a potential confidentiality breach that requires prompt action. Reporting and following the facility's incident-response procedure help limit harm and support appropriate corrective measures.

questions.question_text: A CHPS compound introduces a new appointment reminder system. After three months, missed appointments decrease from 40% to 15%, but the team also finds that some clients receive reminders after their appointment dates. Which conclusion is most appropriate?

choices.text: The intervention has failed completely and should be abandoned immediately
The intervention appears to have improved attendance, but the reminder process requires further review and refinement
The reduction in missed appointments proves that all clients received reminders correctly
The team should stop monitoring appointment attendance

questions.rationale: The reduction in missed appointments suggests that the intervention has had a positive effect on attendance. However, delayed reminders indicate a process weakness that should be investigated and corrected through continued quality improvement.
